reading.body:
CyrusOne's Somerset, New Jersey campus publishes 23 MW of IT capacity across 185,000 square feet, the second-largest disclosed figure in a state where only five of 48 mapped data centers publish power at all.

The disclosure gap is the more useful signal. Five operators reporting 111.3 MW total means New Jersey's published capacity is a floor, not an inventory. Somerset alone is 20.7 percent of that disclosed total, so its rank reflects who reports rather than where the state's power actually sits.

For AI specifically, 23 MW is modest next to hyperscale training clusters. The same floor space yields roughly 575 racks at 40 kW each, or roughly 290 at 80 kW, so the density assumption decides whether this reads as colocation or as AI training space. No certifications are published, so nothing in the data qualifies the campus for particular workloads.

What the data does not cover is tenant base, actual power draw, grid interconnection, and announced expansion, which the suitability score lists as missing. That score of 64 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type. Nothing here establishes whether the campus serves AI workloads at all.
